transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-09
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Arjun Rao (Redwood SE), Lena Wu (Redwood CSM), Daniel Kim (Lumina Head of ML), Sara Lopez (Lumina PM), Rajat Singh (Lumina Security)

Summary:
Quick product walkthrough of Redwood's Eval/Quality Monitoring features (prompt sets, regression alerts, A/B comparisons), discussion of Lumina's evaluation needs, security questions, and next steps to run a short pilot.

Topics covered:
- Prompt set management and versioning
- Regression alerts and baselining
- A/B comparison dashboards and statistical tests
- Integration with CI and production telemetry
- Security/compliance (SOC 2, KMS, audit logs)
- Pilot scope and success criteria

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. quick intros?
[00:08] Daniel Kim: Daniel here, head of ML at Lumina. we run a few clinical summarization flows and want to reduce hallucinations and regression risk.
[00:15] Sara Lopez: Sara, product -- focusing on user-facing notes and triage, timeline is Q3 for pilot.
[00:20] Rajat Singh: Rajat from security, I'll be vetting data residency and KMS stuff.
[00:25] Arjun Rao: Great, I'm Arjun, I'll walk through the demo and show the console, the eval features and how alerts work.
[00:30] Maya Patel: quick note - we'll demo prompting, A/B and the regression alerts; afterwards we'll capture next steps and share the eval template we use.

[02:05] Arjun Rao: ok opening Redwood Console, this is the Eval/Quality tab - you can see prompt sets on the left, each prompt-set is versioned. when you run an eval it stores results and you can label examples. i'll run a small run to show the comparisons.
[02:38] Arjun Rao: so here we've uploaded 120 clinical notes, 4 prompt variants; you can do pairwise A/B or multi-arm comparisons and pick metrics - like F1, rouge, hallucination rate, or our custom rubric.
[03:12] Sara Lopez: quick question - can we plug in our rubric? like a 5-point clinical accuracy score?
[03:18] Arjun Rao: yes, you can upload a JSON rubric or use the UI to create rubrics; results map to your metric. it's also possible to map to downstream KPIs - so you can see token cost vs quality.
[03:45] Daniel Kim: how robust are the statistical tests? we need significance across small sample sizes often.
[03:50] Arjun Rao: we run bootstrap CIs and pairwise t-tests with Bonferroni correction; you can pick the alpha and sample-strategy, and there's automatic power estimation before you run the test.

[05:10] Arjun Rao: next, regression alerts - you can pin a baseline model or prompt-set; we compute a rolling baseline and will fire alerts if the metric drops beyond the configured delta. this ties into your CI - you can block deploys if a regression is detected.
[05:45] Daniel Kim: nice, so we can stop a rollout if the hallucination rate climbs. how are false positives handled?
[05:52] Arjun Rao: you can set a sensitivity window, include manual verification steps, or require multiple consecutive windows before blocking. also alerts can route to Slack, PagerDuty, or create Jira tickets.

[07:20] Sara Lopez: integration wise - can our product telemetry join the evals, like production P95 latency and error traces?
[07:27] Arjun Rao: yes, Redwood Console ingests prod telemetry via our SDK or webhook; you can map inputs to eval examples and see correlation plots - e.g., higher latency with longer prompts correlates with increased halluci... hallu- hallucinations. apologies for stuttering there.

[08:45] Rajat Singh: on security - where is evaluation data stored, and do you support customer-managed keys?
[08:52] Maya Patel: we store data in region you pick, encrypted at rest. Redwood Private offers VPC/on-prem. we support KMS/HSM with customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated, and for Hosted we support CMKs via cloud KMS.
[09:12] Rajat Singh: are audit logs immutable? we need 7 years for certain records.
[09:16] Maya Patel: audit logs are append-only and exportable to your retention system; for Private we can accommodate longer retention and air-gapped export. we'll share the SOC2/ISO pack.

[11:00] Arjun Rao: back to demo - here's an A/B run results page: you can filter by demographic, by templates, even by downstream labeler. there's a waterfall view that shows token cost delta and a small regression in precision on prompt B.
[11:30] Daniel Kim: can we automate rollbacks based on that?
[11:33] Arjun Rao: yes with rollout policies - canary -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback if metrics degrade beyond thresholds.

[13:05] Sara Lopez: our big worry is prompt drift over time as we tweak templates; how do you handle prompt inventory and lineage?
[13:12] Arjun Rao: every prompt-set is versioned and linked to model versions; there's metadata about who edited, commit messages, and you can diff prompt versions. we also store KV cache hints but sometimes the transcriber writes it as K V cache.

[14:50] Arjun Rao: for A/B we also support synthetic augmentations - you can generate adversarial variants and include them in the prompt set to stress-test.
[15:20] Daniel Kim: awesome. what's the typical sample size you recommend for low-variance measurements?
[15:26] Arjun Rao: it depends on your metric; for hallucination binary signals, often 200-500 examples per arm; for fine-grained ordinal rubrics you might need more. Console estimates power for you.

[17:00] Maya Patel: quick commercial note - hosted API pricing is per-token, Dedicated reserved capacity has commit options if you need predictable throughput. we'll include a ballpark for the pilot in the follow-up.
[17:20] Sara Lopez: do you have references in healthcare?
[17:24] Maya Patel: yes, several health customers (anonymized); we can connect you with a reference who ran a similar clinical summarization pilot.

[18:40] Rajat Singh: also need to know about PII handling and retention in logs, can we scrub PHI before it leaves our network?
[18:48] Arjun Rao: yes you can run a pre-processing step in your pipeline to redact/scrub or use Private deployment. we also support in-flight transformations via webhooks for hosted if you want to pseudonymize before storage.

[21:05] Arjun Rao: demo: creating a regression alert - set baseline to model v1.3 and metric = clinical_accuracy, threshold -3% from baseline over 48h window, route alert to security channel.
[21:40] Sara Lopez: what about multiple baselines for different cohorts? e.g., cardiology vs primary care?
[21:46] Arjun Rao: yes cohorts supported; you can define segment filters and maintain separate baselines per cohort.

[24:10] Daniel Kim: if we run the A/B in the console and then want to push the winner to production, how seamless is the flow?
[24:18] Arjun Rao: one-click promote; it creates a release artifact with prompt-set and model pins; can be tied into your CI for deploy gating.

[26:00] Maya Patel: ok let's talk pilot scope — Lena, maybe you can help?
[26:05] Lena Wu: sure. proposed pilot: 1-week A/B with 2 prompt variants, 500 examples each, run our hallucination plus accuracy rubric, integrate alerts to Slack, and a short benchmark for latency. success metrics: lower hallucination by 25% in winning arm and no regression in latency >10%.
[26:35] Sara Lopez: that aligns with our Q3 decision criteria. timeline wise we need security sign-off by mid-June.

[28:00] Rajat Singh: i can review the security materials; please send the default data flow diagram and KMS integration notes.
[28:07] Maya Patel: will do. we'll also send the SOC2 package and the sample prompt-set template.

[30:10] Arjun Rao: quick note on cost controls - Redwood Optimize suggests batching and quantization profiles; for inference we can recommend a quantized model that reduces cost with minimal quality delta and you can evaluate that in the same A/B. sometimes people call it Redwood Optima in docs, small typo i've seen.

[31:40] Daniel Kim: curious about reproducibility - if we re-run an eval in 6 months, will prompt-set versions and model pins reproduce exact outputs?
[31:48] Arjun Rao: yes if you pin model version and seed; for nondeterministic ops we'll surface sample seeds and you can snapshot the entire eval artifact.

[33:10] Sara Lopez: any gotchas for HIPAA workloads specifically?
[33:18] Maya Patel: main items are data residency, BAAs, and auditability; Private deployment is typical for PHI full coverage. we'll start with hosted evals on de-identified data.

[35:00] Daniel Kim: ok, financials - can you include pilot pricing?
[35:06] Maya Patel: yes we'll include a pilot quote; usually it's a time-limited trial tenant plus usage estimate.

[37:20] Arjun Rao: demo wrap-up - will attach the prompt-set we used, sample rubric, and the benchmark scripts.

[38:05] Maya Patel: anything else from Lumina?
[38:12] Sara Lopez: please include a sample A/B dashboard screenshot and the exportable CSV schema.
[38:20] Rajat Singh: add details on KMS and retention.

[40:00] Maya Patel: recap / next steps: 1) we'll send eval guide, security pack, and pricing (Maya). 2) Arjun will share benchmark scripts and prompt-set KB. 3) Rajat to send retention requirements. 4) schedule POC run for week of 2026-06-16.
[40:25] Daniel Kim: thanks all, this was helpful. we'll confirm the timeline internally and reply on the thread.
[40:30] Maya Patel: great, thanks everyone, we'll follow up by end of day tomorrow.

[45:50] Call end.
